sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Dunedin, FL?
sections.html:
Yes. A Dunedin house can change hands quickly when the buyer pays cash and accepts the home as it stands, and the paperwork needed to close is the same short list of Florida documents that any sale uses. What takes time is usually the house itself: repairs, a tenant, a probate case or a lender deadline.

Dunedin sits on the Gulf side of Pinellas County, just north of Clearwater and St. Petersburg. The city says it is one of the few open waterfront communities between Sarasota and Cedar Key where buildings do not block the view of the water. A cash sale lets you skip the repair-request negotiation that follows a buyer's inspection.

This page walks through how Dunedin is laid out, what a sale costs at the county and state level, the Pinellas homestead rules that affect the next owner's tax bill, and the steps to record a deed.

sections.h2: Who buys homes in Dunedin and why?
sections.html:
Dunedin is a small Gulf-coast city with a walkable downtown, a Scottish naming tradition and a steady stream of visitors. The city's own history page says the area was first called Jonesboro, after the owner of a local general store, and that Scottish merchants asked for a post office named Dunedin in 1882. Dunedin became an incorporated town on June 1, 1899 and a city in 1925.

The city reports a population above 35,000 as of 2025. Street and neighborhood names such as Scotland Street, Louden Avenue and Brae-Moor reflect that heritage, and buyers who know the area tend to look for homes near the downtown, the waterfront parks or the Pinellas Trail. Dunedin was the first Florida city to earn the Trail Town designation, according to the city.

  • Honeymoon Island State Park is reached from Dunedin by the causeway.
  • Dunedin is the Spring Training home of the Toronto Blue Jays at TD Ballpark.
  • The city lists its golf club on the state and national historic registers.

The seller's takeaway: interest comes from three groups: people who want to live near the downtown, people who want a second home near the beaches, and investors. A cash buyer can serve all three without asking you to stage the house or schedule open houses.

sections.h2: What does selling a house cost in Dunedin?
sections.html:
The costs that come from the state and county are fixed by law, so you can check them before you list. The largest is usually the documentary stamp tax on the deed, which the Florida Department of Revenue prints as 70 cents on each $100 of consideration for every county except Miami-Dade.

Under the state's rule, every party to the document is liable for the tax, whichever party agrees to pay it. In a standard contract the seller pays. Have the figure shown on your closing statement before you sign.

The clerk also charges to record the deed. Florida Statutes section 28.24 lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus a technology charge of $4 per page and a small modernization trust fund charge. Pinellas County's clerk can confirm the current total for your deed.

sections.h2: How do Pinellas County homestead rules affect a Dunedin sale?
sections.html:
The Pinellas County Property Appraiser handles homestead exemptions, and the office's page prints the current benefit as $51,411 off assessed value. The first $25,000 applies to every tax on the bill, and the remaining $26,411 applies to the value between $50,000 and $75,000 and leaves out school taxes.

A sale ends the seller's homestead. The appraiser's page lists a sale, a rental, a change of ownership and moving out as reasons the exemption stops. If you bought after January 1 and your notice of proposed taxes still shows a homestead, that exemption belongs to the prior owner and is removed on December 31. The new owner must file an original application by March 1 to get it for the following year.

The state's Save Our Homes cap also resets on a sale. The Florida Department of Revenue says the property goes back to just value on the next January 1 after a change of ownership, so the buyer's first full-year bill can be higher than the seller's. If you are moving to another Florida home, ask the appraiser about portability. The new homestead must be established within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, and the transfer application is due by March 1.

sections.h2: What documents does a Dunedin deed need?
sections.html:
A Florida deed must be in writing and signed in front of two witnesses, and no seal is needed. Section 689.01 also allows witnessing by audio-video technology. A title company or attorney usually prepares the deed and files it for you.

A typical Dunedin closing runs in this order:

  1. Sign the purchase contract and open a title order.
  2. Clear any liens, mortgage payoffs or open permits found in the title search.
  3. Sign the deed in front of two witnesses.
  4. Pay the documentary stamps and recording charges at the clerk.
  5. Update the tax roll through the property appraiser after recording.

If the house passes through an estate, the personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable for doc stamps. Quitclaim deeds, deeds in lieu of foreclosure and contracts for deed are taxable, so a family transfer by quitclaim can still carry a tax bill.

sections.h2: What if I owe back taxes or am behind on the mortgage in Dunedin?
sections.html:
You still have options, but the dates matter. Florida property tax bills go out in November, and the state prints an early-payment discount that steps down from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and the tax collector sells tax certificates by June 1.

On the lender side, a foreclosure judgment is followed by a public sale not less than 20 days or more than 35 days after judgment, unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer period. The high bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale. If you are behind, selling before judgment is the route that keeps any equity in your hands, and any surplus after a sale is claimed through the clerk.

  • Ask the Pinellas County Tax Collector about installment or deferral programs.
  • Ask your lender for a payoff letter before you accept an offer.
  • Ask the clerk how to claim surplus funds if a sale has already occurred.

sections.h2: How should I decide between a cash sale and listing in Dunedin?
sections.html:
Compare the net, not the headline price. A listing can bring a higher price, but it adds showings, inspection repair requests, buyer financing risk and carrying costs while the house sits. A cash purchase is quicker and the buyer accepts the property as is.

Walk through your own numbers with the closing statement the title company prepares. Include the mortgage payoff, the doc stamps, recording, any unpaid property tax and the cost of repairs you would otherwise make. Ask a local agent, or search the Pinellas County Property Appraiser's public records, for recent sales near your street.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax when a Dunedin house sells?
faqs.a: By contract it is usually the seller, but the state says all parties to the document are liable whichever side agrees to pay. The clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded, at 70 cents per $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The exemption ends with the sale, and the new owner has to file an original application with the Pinellas County Property Appraiser by March 1. A homestead still showing on a notice after you purchase is removed on December 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Dunedin house while it has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes, but the lease and notice rules still apply. Under Florida law a month-to-month tenancy ends with at least 30 days' notice before the end of the monthly period. Check your lease for the terms that carry over to a new owner.

faqs.q: What happens to Save Our Homes when I sell?
faqs.a: The cap does not carry to the buyer. A change of ownership resets the property to just value the next January 1. You may be able to move your own benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability within three years.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Dunedin property?
faqs.a: With the Pinellas County Clerk of the Circuit Court, which collects the stamp tax and the per-page recording charges. Your title company normally files it for you.
